name: Acrokeratoderma

criteria.description: Transient whitish papules and plaques on palms after water exposure
Palmar skin thickening and keratoderma-like changes
Resolution of lesions after drying of skin
Exclusion of other hereditary or acquired keratodermas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of transient palmar hyperwrinkling and palmar skin thickening after water exposure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; biopsy and genetic testing may be supportive but are not routinely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient whitish papules and plaques on palms after water exposure
searchTerms: white bumps on palms after water
temporary pale spots on hands when wet
whitish skin patches on palms after soaking

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapid palmar skin wrinkling within minutes of water contact
searchTerms: fast skin wrinkling on palms with water
rapid palm skin changes after wetting
palm skin hardening similar to keratoderma
slight palm redness in affected times

common.symptomName: Pruritus or burning sensation on affected areas
searchTerms: itching or burning on skin areas
skin irritation with itch or burn

common.symptomName: Lesions resolving within 30 minutes after drying
searchTerms: lesions clear within 30 minutes when dry

occasional.symptomName: Involvement of plantar surfaces with similar changes
Associated mild pain on palmar surfaces

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of affected skin
Extension of lesions to dorsal hands
searchTerms: lesions spreading to back of hands
skin changes extending to dorsal hands

rare.symptomName: Associated nail changes such as thickening or ridging
searchTerms: nail changes like thickening or lines

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis and mild acanthosis
genetic: Possible mutations in genes related to skin barrier function (e.g., AQP5 in some cases)
other: Rapid onset and resolution of lesions after water exposure is diagnostic

distinguishingFeatures: Urticarial wheals rather than keratoderma-like plaques
Lesions persist longer after water exposure
Persistent thickening without transient water-induced changes
Lesions do not resolve rapidly after drying

redFlags: Signs of secondary infection (e.g., purulence, increased erythema)
Rapid progression or involvement beyond typical palmar areas
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Aquagenic acrokeratoderma: clinical features and review. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017;76(2):e39-e40.
